source_text:
Solutiones (fragmentum e tractatu de dogmatum solutione) (e cod. Vat.
gr. 447)
Ηʹ. Ἄνθρωπός τις ἦν πλούσιος, εὐφραινόμενος καθ' ἡμέραν λαμπρῶς·
πτωχὸς δέ τις Λάζαρος ἐπὶ τὸν τούτου πυλῶνα ἐβέβλητο ἡλκωμένος κατὰ τὴν
εὐαγγελικὴν ἱστορίαν. ἐγένετο οὖν ἀμφοτέροις ἀποθανεῖν καὶ τοῦτον μὲν τὸν
πτωχὸν εἰς τὴν ἀνάπαυσιν ἀπελθεῖν, τὸν δὲ εἰς τὴν κόλασιν.
thought_title: The rich man and Lazarus: their opposite fates
orientation: Cyril opens his treatise by summarizing the gospel story of the rich man and Lazarus and their opposite fates after death.
pass_a_gloss: There was a certain rich man, rejoicing daily in splendor; and a certain poor man Lazarus had been laid at his gate, covered with sores, according to the gospel story. It happened therefore for both to die, and this poor man to go away into the rest, but the other into the punishment.

choices.why: keeps the adverbial force of λαμπρῶς as the manner of the daily rejoicing, matching the gospel's picture of lavish living
rejected: making merry every day in splendor

choices.english: had been laid at his gate
choices.why: the pluperfect passive of βάλλω conveys a state resulting from being placed there, and 'laid' preserves the passive force without implying violence
rejected: had been thrown at his gate

choices.why: the perfect participle of ἑλκόω describes his ongoing bodily condition, and 'covered with sores' renders the passive state plainly

choices.english: It happened therefore for both to die
choices.why: keeps the impersonal ἐγένετο with the dative of person and the infinitive, preserving the narrative turn exactly
rejected: So it came about that both died

choices.english: but the other into the punishment
choices.why: the article ὁ δέ is used substantivally for the rich man, and the glossary term κόλασις is rendered 'punishment' as required
rejected: but the rich man into punishment

bible_refs.note: Ἄνθρωπός τις ἦν πλούσιος ... πτωχὸς δέ τις ὀνόματι Λάζαρος ... ἡλκωμένος ... ἀποθανεῖν ... εἰς τὸν κόλπον Ἀβραάμ

pass_b_english: There was a rich man who rejoiced daily in splendor, and a poor man named Lazarus had been laid at his gate, covered with sores, according to the gospel story. It happened, then, that both died, and the poor man departed into rest, but the other into punishment.
